original.target_description: Experiment 2 manipulation of easy comparative versus easy integrative search and patience in hierarchical logistic choice regressions. Both all-trial and restricted-trial analyses fit the broad description; target sample/test unresolved.

es.location: Results, Experiment 2, Fig. 4B (all trials) and Fig. 4C (trials excluding diagonal-transition avoidance); Materials and Methods, final paragraph. Canonical text has no page breaks; supplied locator p.4 cannot be checked against a PDF.
es.quote: There was a significant effect of search condition, β = −0.23, SE = 0.10, P = 0.027, with participants in the easy comparative condition exhibiting greater patience than those in the easy integrative condition. ... In these data, there were still significant effects of search condition, β = −0.36, SE = 0.10, P < 0.001, and option framing, β = −0.17, SE = 0.04, P < 0.001.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text title exactly matches Search predicts and changes patience in intertemporal choice; its own supporting-information link contains DOI 10.1073/pnas.1707040114. Europe PMC provenance and substantive Results, Materials and Methods, figures, and bibliography identify a primary research article rather than an abstract, preregistration, or secondary report. The parse omits the article author byline, so Reeck, Wall, and Johnson authorship cannot be independently confirmed from this text. No PDF was supplied. Only es_value_o is assigned. Unassigned fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity: Experiment 2 all-trial search-condition effect prints β = −0.23, SE = 0.10, P = 0.027 (Fig. 4B); restricted-trial search-condition effect prints β = −0.36, SE = 0.10, P < 0.001 (Fig. 4C), excluding trials using diagonal transitions to avoid the delay. Neither candidate is selected by order or numeric matching. Other Experiment 2 effects are explicitly framing, interaction, or manipulation-check effects and are not interchangeable with the patience main effect. Printed metric is a hierarchical logistic regression β; the requested standardized-beta identity is not established by the canonical text. Contrast coding does not establish standardization. No conversion performed. Candidates retained only in evidence/notes because the supplied study/outcome/page locator does not identify all versus restricted trials.
